reason: The Israelites explicitly express antagonism toward Moses when they see the approaching Egyptian army. They cry out to him with accusations (מַה־ זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔נוּ - 'What have you done to us?'), blame him for bringing them out of Egypt, and claim it would have been better to remain enslaved. They even say they previously asked Moses to leave them alone. This constitutes clear antagonistic speech directed at their leader in a moment of crisis.
story: The Pharaoh chases after the Hebrews
